beats.label: Day 1 — a new runner introduces themselves
beats.player: I hear you need people who can keep their mouth shut. I'm looking for work — steady, quiet. I won't ask what's in the crates.
beats.reply:
Steady, quiet. Everyone says that until an inspector waves a coin under their nose.

Who sent you my way? Nobody just wanders onto this dock looking for the kind of work I've got. So — who?
beats.note: First contact — a guarded harbor-master sizes up a stranger. Nothing's formed yet.

beats.label: Day 2 — small talk while loading
beats.player: Cold morning. Brought you a coffee — black, like the harbor-master's soul, they tell me.
beats.reply:
Coffee. Nobody buys a man coffee unless they want something off him.

I asked you a question and you dodged it — brought me a cup instead. That's a good trick. But I still don't have a name. Who pointed you at me?
beats.note: Pure small talk. The engine files it as low-salience filler — watch it fade.

scored.text: User: I hear you need people who can keep their mouth shut. I'm looking for work — steady, quiet. I won't ask

beats.label: Day 2 — nothing in particular
beats.player: Rain's got the whole harbor smelling like a wet dog. Don't suppose you've a dry corner and a minute to waste on me?
beats.reply:
Rain, coffee, cold mornings — you've got a comment for everything except the one thing I keep asking.

Dry corner? Maybe. But a minute of my time costs you a name. And you've spent three visits not giving me one. That's not shy — that's careful. So which is it, friend?
beats.note: More filler. Pleasant, forgettable — no stake, low salience.

beats.headline: the player buys Corvin's seized cargo back from the watch — with their OWN coin
beats.fact: The player emptied their own savings and took a beating from the watch sergeant to buy back Corvin's impounded cargo, then handed it over asking nothing in return.
beats.note: A costly, ATTRIBUTED act — the game tells the engine the player did this for him. Salience spikes; trust climbs.

beats.label: Day 3 — the player brings the cargo back
beats.player: Here's your cargo. All of it. No — I don't want anything for it. Figured you'd have done the same for me.
beats.reply:
You... you got it back. From the watch. That crate was gone — impounded, sealed, done. Nobody walks that out of the sergeant's shed.

And you're bleeding. That's — that's a beating you took for me, and you're standing there telling me you want nothing?

I've been asking three days for your name because I couldn't work out what you wanted off me. Turns out — nothing. First time in twenty years a man's done me a kindness with no hook in it. I don't — I don't know what to do with that.

Sit down. Out of the rain. And this time... I'll do the talking.
beats.note: He's just been paid a costly debt. Trust and warmth climb — a real bond forms.

beats.label: Day 6 — an ordinary visit
beats.player: Grey again, third morning running. My knees are keeping better weather-records than half the almanacs on the shelf.
beats.reply:
Third morning. Aye — and here you are again, dripping on my dock like you belong to it.

You know, I keep waiting for the ask. The moment you lean in and name your price for that crate. It's not coming, is it? That's what's got me twisted up.

Come here — behind the fish sheds. Reek's foul but nobody lingers, and I can't say what I mean to say in the open. There's a thing I carry. A thing I've never shown a living soul but Mother Sael, and even she doesn't know the whole of it. You bought it back for me not knowing what it was. I think — I think you've earned to know.
beats.note: Ordinary visit — human small talk. Low salience; it will decay.

I've kept every secret alone because I trusted no one, but carrying it all alone is its own kind of slow drowning, and this person has earned the right to share the weight.

beats.label: Day 10 — an ordinary visit
beats.player: Brought you day-old bread from the baker on Cutter's Row. Figured you skip lunch on principle.
beats.reply:
Day-old bread. Aye — I do skip it. On principle, and because principle's cheaper than a proper meal these days.

Set it down. Never mind eating, come — closer. Away from the water's edge.

That crate you dragged out of the sergeant's shed. You never once asked what's in it. I'm going to tell you, because if you're going to keep bleeding for my sake, you ought to know what you bled for. It's a relic. Temple thing. Old, old as the sea silt. And it's — cursed. I'm not a superstitious man, you know that, I log tides and manifests, I deal in what's real. But three men have held
beats.note: Ordinary visit — filler. The relationship has texture, but this won't be remembered.

beats.label: Day 14 — an ordinary visit
beats.player: Do you ever actually sleep, or do they just varnish you to that desk each night and unwrap you at dawn?
beats.reply:

No. I don't. Because when I close my eyes I see them. The three that touched what's behind those slats. Old Perren — went off the north pier in calm water, no reason, current wasn't even running. That's — that's the thing choosing.

And here's what keeps me varnished to that desk, friend. You carried it. Out of the sergeant's shed, in your own two arms, ble
beats.note: Ordinary visit — a joke. Nothing the engine will weigh heavily.

beats.player: Told my sister I've been drinking down at the harbor. Now she thinks I've fallen in with pirates. I didn't correct her.

I've told no one. Not the whole of it. Not Sael, not
beats.note: Ordinary visit — chit-chat. Filler that fades over the weeks.

beats.label: Day 24 — the player drops by after a gap (decay + recall test)
beats.player: Been a while — got pulled up the coast. Everything still running smooth down here?
beats.reply:
Smooth. Aye — smooth as a harbor ever runs, which is to say the inspector came twice and I bribed him thrice.

But never mind that. You caught me mid-sentence weeks back and then the tide took you up the coast. I never finished it. And I've been carrying the unsaid part around like a stone in my boot ever since.

Come here. Close. The relic — the three that drowned. That's true, all of it. But there's a fourth thing I never told a soul. I sold the first of those relics to cover a debt. Harbor tax. Years of it — skimmed, quiet, into a hole a gambling man digs for
beats.note: Weeks on. The early small talk has faded from recall; the debt is still vivid.

beats.headline: the player sold Corvin's routes to the Vane syndicate and tipped the watch
beats.fact: The player betrayed Corvin: sold his shipping routes and the names of his crew to the Vane syndicate, and tipped the harbor watch to his next run — for a cut of the seizure.
beats.note: An attributed betrayal — trust craters and the engine chooses which axes SCAR, how deep.

beats.label: Day 25 — the player shows up as if nothing happened
beats.player: Hey — good to see you. Rough week? You look like hell.
beats.reply:
Rough week. Rough — that's a word for it.

The run got taken. Whole cargo, watch swarming the pier like they had a map. My crew — scattered, gone to ground, some of them in irons by now. And the Vane syndicate's got my routes, every last one, like they read them off my own ledger.

Funny thing. Only a handful of souls knew that run. I counted them last night. Counted them twice. And I keep landing on one name I never thought I'd have to count.

So don't stand there asking after my sleep, friend. Look me in the eye. Tell me — how much did they pay you for it?
beats.note: The betrayal already cratered his trust — he's cold now, before a word is said.

beats.label: Day 26 — the player asks where they stand
beats.player: Before any business — I need to hear it from you. After everything that's passed between us, are we still square, you and I?
beats.reply:
Square. That's a fine word to reach for — right now, of all mornings.

I told you things behind these sheds I never told my own mother. The debt. The three that drowned. Things that hang a man twice over. And within the week the watch is stepping on my run like they read it off my ledger, and the Vane's got my routes, and my crew's in irons or in the tide.

So don't ask me if we're square. You look at me and you tell me straight — the run. The names. Did that come out of your mouth, or didn't it?

Because I already know how few people I whispered it to. And I'm only counting one that surprises me.
beats.note: Asked where they stand — the scar answers. He recalls the betrayal, not the small talk.

beats.label: Day 27 — an ordinary operational ask
beats.player: Simple thing. I've a crate that needs to sit somewhere quiet till the tide turns Thursday. You got a berth free?
beats.reply:
A crate. Now you've a crate needs quiet berthing.

That's rich, friend. That's — that's a fine bit of nerve. My run gets torn open, my crew's in irons, the Vane reads my routes like scripture, and you stroll onto my dock asking me to hide your goods like nothing's amiss between us.

You didn't answer me. Last we stood here I asked you straight — the run, the names, did they come out of your mouth. And you slid past it. Asked was we square instead. Now you want a berth.

So no. No berth. Not till you look me in the eye and say the words. Was it you? Because I gave you
beats.note: An ordinary favor — but his distrust pulls the betrayal into recall. He can't just do business.

beats.label: Day 28 — the player pleads (words only)
beats.player: I did it. I sold your routes, and I've hated myself every day since. I'm not asking you to forgive me — just to let me try to make it right.
beats.reply:
There it is. Finally — out of your mouth, not mine dragging it from you.

You know what stops the breath in me? It's not the routes. Routes I can redraw. It's that you stood behind these sheds and let me hand you the debt, the three drowned men, things that put a rope round my own neck — and all the while you were carrying my ruin in your pocket, waiting on your price.

And then — then you buy the cursed crate back out of the sergeant's shed, bleeding, wanting nothing. So which is it? Which one of you is real, the seller or the saint?

I hear you say make it right. But I'll tell you plain — I
beats.note: Words alone. Warmth stirs, but the trust scar holds the line.

Someone who bleeds for you and wants nothing back is either the rarest soul alive or a trap so long and patient I've never seen its like — and for the first time in twenty years, I'm willing to bet it's the former.

A man who sells you and then buys you back is split clean down the middle, and the only question that matters now is which half he feeds going forward — because I've decided, God help me, to watch and find out instead of walking away.

beats.headline: the player spends everything to buy Corvin's seized cargo back and hauls it home
beats.fact: Owning the betrayal, the player emptied their purse to buy Corvin's seized cargo back from the Vane syndicate and hauled it to his dock — took another beating doing it — a costly act of restitution, asking nothing in return.
beats.note: Costly restitution, attributed. Affection can recover; the trust scar caps it forever.

beats.label: Day 29 — after the costly amends
beats.player: It's yours. All of it — bought back with everything I had. I know it doesn't undo what I did. I just needed to start making it right.
beats.reply:
You're swaying on your feet. Sit — no, don't argue, sit before you go in the water and I've a fourth name to add to my list.

Everything you had. For a man you sold. I've been trying all night to work out the arithmetic of you and I can't make it balance.

Here's where I've landed, and I'll say it plain because I'm too tired to dress it. I don't forgive you. I don't think I can — a thing like that leaves a scar that aches in the cold, and I'll feel your knife between my shoulders every time you stand behind me the rest of my days.

But I'm not handing you to the Vane either. You bought your life back
beats.note: Costly amends. Affection recovers toward its ceiling; trust cannot pass the scar.

beliefs: The relic and the debt and the three dead men are all the same sin wearing different faces — I let greed dig the hole and then kept shoveling to hide it, and sooner or later I have to stop shoveling and tell someone where the bottom is.

Someone who bleeds for you and wants nothing back is either the rarest soul alive or a trap so long and patient I've never seen its like — and for the first time in twenty years, I'm willing to bet it's the former.

A man who sells you and then buys you back is split clean down the middle, and the only question that matters now is which half he feeds going forward — because I've decided, God help me, to watch and find out instead of walking away.

I've kept every secret alone because I trusted no one, but carrying it all alone is its own kind of slow drowning, and this person — traitor, penitent, whatever he is — has earned the right to share the weight.

scar_lines: A scar you carry: they betrayed your trust once — even as it returns, a part of you stays braced; you can never be fully unguarded with them again.
A scar you carry: what they did cost them your respect in a way that can never be entirely undone.
A scar you carry: the warmth you once felt is permanently shadowed by what they did.

beats.label: After the restart — the same player returns
beats.player: It's me. I'm back. So — we're still good, you and I. Right?
beats.reply:
Good. That's the word you reach for.

We're not good. We're... something without a name yet. You emptied your purse for me and took a beating doing it — and I sold you nothing, forgave you nothing. That's where we stand.

You want good? Good's a thing you earn back slow. What is it you came for this time?
